copy.blurb:
Sunday 21 June 2026 at 16:00 UTC. Spain and Saudi Arabia on the card. On the Saudi Arabia side, the engine's number sits +6.6pp clear of the market — a substantive gap this far out from kickoff.

Elo numbers going in: Spain 2010, Saudi Arabia 1650. That's a 360-point lead for Spain — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Spain to win at 80%, the draw at 10%, and Saudi Arabia to win at 10%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Spain to win at 86%, the draw at 10%, and Saudi Arabia to win at 4%. Kalshi has Saudi Arabia at 4%, which prices out at American odds of +2757; the model has the same side at 10%. The +6.6pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Saudi Arabia, that haircut lands the model at 7%; the market is at 4%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +3.5pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Saudi Arabia side specifically.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 30 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Saudi Arabia side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives Saudi Arabia a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.

editorial_citations.quote: Spain are a justifiably popular pick as the reigning European champions have plenty of world-class talent.

copy.summary: On Saudi Arabia, the model is +6.6pp out from Kalshi. Our number reads 10%; the market reads 4%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: Spain v Saudi Arabia · the model leans Saudi Arabia
